title: Match Fourier coefficients and odd-length frequency bins to the DFT convention
body:
## Problem
`DFT` builds the documented negative-exponent Fourier basis but evaluates it with `np.vdot`, which conjugates that basis. This reverses complex phase and gives incorrect coefficients for complex-valued inputs. `dft_bins(..., positive_only=True)` also places the final frequency at Nyquist for odd-length frames, even though their last DFT bin is below Nyquist.

## Change
Evaluate the existing Fourier basis with matrix multiplication, and generate positive frequencies as `k * fs / N`. These changes make coefficient values and their frequency coordinates follow the same DFT convention. Existing real-signal magnitude and power behavior remains covered.

## Validation
- The 35 new tests against unchanged upstream: 17 failed, 18 passed.
- New tests plus the existing DFT test: 36 passed on Python 3.9.25.
- References include NumPy FFT/frequency helpers, a hard-coded four-point sine phase, real/complex inputs, odd/even/singleton lengths, and magnitude/power controls.
- Independent read-only review found no blockers.
- Existing full preprocessing tests have three unrelated Librosa 0.11 reference-call incompatibilities; the new frequency tests use NumPy rather than those incompatible calls.
